I farm 8 mu here in Quzhou, same as I always do — wheat in winter, maize after. My man and I have done this thirty years. Two of our children work in town so it is mostly me and him in the field. My neighbors all plant the same way so I just follow what works on our road.

For wheat, I plant after the maize comes off in October. I buy the good seed from the dealer in town — the one my neighbor Wang's wife uses, she had a good crop last year. I put down 2 bags of compound fertilizer per mu when I sow — that is one hundred jin. In spring when the wheat greens up and starts to joint, I put one bag of urea per mu on top, maybe a little more because I do not want the wheat to look yellow. My husband will not hear of a thin crop. I water three times from the well — once after planting if dry, once at jointing with the urea, once when the grain is filling. I spray twice, once for aphids and once for the red disease on the heads. I plough after maize to turn in the stalks.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June, no time to plough, I just drill into the stubble. I use hybrid seed, same kind as last year, it gave me good ears. I put one and a half bags of compound at sowing and then one bag of urea when the maize is knee-high. I water once or twice if the rain does not come. I spray once for the borer worm and once for weeds. Last year I got about 1100 jin of maize per mu and 900 jin of wheat, so I expect the same.

I do not skip fertilizer to save money — a poor harvest costs more than the extra bag. That is what my mother-in-law taught me.
